VALUE SOURCE: a PURE defensive/utility kit — ZERO of her five lines touch damage dealt, so the override encodes NOTHING: empty blocks on all three slots, every line documented verbatim under unmodeled. Her only sim-visible footprint is her rotation body: the sole Burst I on her board row, casting every ~20s chain on the default gauge path (burstGaugePerShot from characters.json; she is not in data/gauge-per-shot.json and no kit line modifies gauge). S1 'Professional Origami' (cd 15s) restores 17.76% Cover HP to all allies and removes 1 debuff from 2 random debuffed allies — cover HP is the team's COVER resource, not unit HP, and v1 models no HP/cover pool and no ally debuffs. S2 'Professional Tomato Sauce' stacks self Damage Taken ▼4.37% per full-charge attack (15 stacks, 5 sec) — v1 models no incoming damage, and its ONLY consumer is the burst's max-stacks gate, unmodeled together with the line it feeds. Burst 'Professional Maid Leader' removes 1 debuff from all allies and — gated on Tomato Sauce at max stacks — drops all enemies' ATK by 13.59% for 10 sec; enemy ATK ▼ debuffs are dropped at dispatch (no incoming-damage model — the boss never attacks into our numbers; the enemy-buff allowlist admits damageTakenPct/distributedDamagePct/defPct only, and this line is ATK ▼, not DEF ▼), and the gate's stacking resource does not exist in v1. EVIDENCE TIER: all magnitudes are kit-text-literal (SL10 datamine); every line is out-of-domain for a damage-dealt sim, so there are no live values to hand-tune. Kit-autonomy gauntlet 2026-08-03.
caveats: ⚑ Cover-HP restore (17.76% of Cover HP, all allies, skill1 cd 15s) is UNMODELED, tier out-of-domain (no cover/HP pool in v1). It is NOT encoded as a `heal` effect on purpose: cover repair is not HP recovery in the kit's own terms, and a heal would emit recovery events that fire teammates' on-recovery consumers (e.g. crown's 'when recovery takes effect') — a synergy cocoa does not have. Whether in-game cover repair fires on-recovery triggers is UNMEASURED; the default is no-emit, and flipping that default needs a measurement, not a prior. Recipe if a cover pool is ever modeled: emit a cover-restore event on skill1's 15s clock, no recovery trigger.

⚑ Debuff removal (skill1: 1 debuff from 2 random debuffed allies; burst: 1 debuff from all allies) is UNMODELED, tier out-of-domain: v1 models no ally debuffs (the boss deals no damage and applies none), so there is nothing to cleanse. Recipe if ally debuffs are ever modeled: cleanse 1 on skill1's 15s clock (2 random debuffed holders) and 1 on cocoa's OWN burstCast (all allies — burstCast, not fullBurstEnter).

⚑ Self Damage Taken ▼4.37% per full-charge attack (15 stacks, 5 sec) is UNMODELED, tier out-of-domain: v1 models no incoming damage, so a damage-taken modifier has no consumer. Estimate if it ever mattered: with SR cadence (60-frame charge, 6 ammo, 141 reload) stacks would saturate ~25-30s into the fight and stay up (UNMEASURED derivation). Its only consumer is the burst's max-stacks gate — both are unmodeled together. Nearest-wrong encoding to avoid: the schema's damageTakenPct is a BOSS debuff (positive = boss takes MORE damage); writing this self ▼ line onto the boss would swing team damage up to 15×4.37% ≈ 65.55%.

⚑ Enemy ATK ▼13.59% for 10 sec, gated on Tomato Sauce at max stacks at cast time, is UNMODELED, tier out-of-domain: enemy ATK ▼ is dropped at dispatch — the boss never attacks into our numbers (no incoming-damage model), so an ATK ▼ has no consumer (this is NOT the enemy DEF ▼ channel; the kit line is ATK ▼). It is NOT damageTakenPct (that is 'boss takes more damage' — a different mechanic). Recipe if boss attacks are ever modeled: 10s ATK-down on all enemies, applied only when the caster holds 15 Tomato stacks at her own burstCast.

Zero damage lines, zero weapon-state modifiers, zero gauge modifiers in the whole kit — cocoa cannot move her own or any teammate's damage. Her committed override is byte-identical in effect to the bare weapon: the board value is entirely defensive and lives outside v1's domain. Any future edit that adds an effect to this file is an over-encoding unless it cites a new primitive + measurement.
